title: Plan drafted from PM-tool-as-backlog crossover + adapter setup friction concerns
body: Two concerns surfaced during P10 F003 Linear-pick conversation: (1) If Linear (or any PM tool — Aha, Jira, Monday, GitHub Projects) holds operator's cross-platform plan backlog, DontPanic plan status drifts instantly from PM-tool issue status — crossover with the dashboard is real. (2) Adapter setup is 4 manual steps today; if operators want to wire 5+ services each one costs identical friction. Setup bloat real concern. Initial draft bundled dashboard ship + category contract + sync + CLI into one plan. Operator review (D003) split that into clean ownership boundaries.

title: Scoping principle: category contract, not per-service core code
body: DontPanic owns a PM-tool category contract (abstract Issue/Project/Status/Comment models + sync hooks). Each service supplies a PP-generated MCP adapter PLUS a small semantic mapping config that translates the service's concepts to the abstract contract. No DontPanic core code is added per service unless the category contract itself expands. Service-specific concepts (Linear cycles, Jira epics, Monday boards) are NOT in the abstraction; they surface via the raw MCP adapter as opaque pass-throughs. This is the primary lock-in mitigator + the primary protection against config bloat — if operator adds 5 PM tools they author 5 small JSONs + 5 thin Python wrapper modules (≤100 lines each), not 5 service-specific abstractions in core.

title: Pre-lock review pivot: removed F001 dashboard ship + F004 CLI; narrowed to 3 features
body: Operator review of initial 4-feature draft surfaced: schema blocker (missing description, invalid surface enum); double-ownership of P9-004 work (F001 dashboard ship pulled into this plan creates ownership ambiguity); overclaim on 'config-only' PM tool addition (Jira/Linear/Monday/Aha shapes don't share enough for field-mapping-only; each needs ~100-line wrapper module); CLI premature (build the contract + prove one adapter works manually first); external mutation risk underspecified (status push needs durable evidence, dry-run, opt-in). Revised plan: drop F001 dashboard ship (stays in P9-004 ownership; this plan depends on it externally); reword 'config-only' claim as 'category contract + small wrapper per service'; replace linked_issue_id with external_refs[] array (kind/uri/sync); strengthen mutation safety (every write produces durable evidence record, no silent warnings, dry-run path, retry via resync); defer dontpanic adapter add CLI to follow-on plan after one adapter validates the abstraction. Final shape: F001 PM-tool category contract + Linear reference, F002 external_refs + sync layer with durable evidence, F003 dashboard linked-status chip (depends on P9-004 completion).

title: Schema validation blockers resolved
body: Initial draft plan.md failed plan.schema.json v1.0 validation: (a) missing required 'description' field; (b) surfaces.1='dashboard' not in valid enum (web/ios/android/backend/infra/security/data/ux/ml/docs/external-api-wrap). Fixed: added description block to frontmatter (min 10 chars; explains the bridge's bounded scope); surfaces=[infra, external-api-wrap, web]. The 'web' surface covers the dashboard linked-status chip in F003; 'external-api-wrap' covers the PM-tool adapter integration; 'infra' covers the category contract code paths.

title: External mutation safety: every push produces durable evidence
body: F002's external_refs sync layer pushes DontPanic status to PM-tool issues on plan close. This is a real side effect on a third-party system; failures must be observable + retriable. Locked requirements: (1) sync field on external_ref is explicit opt-in (sync: none|push_status; default none). (2) `dontpanic plan close --dry-run` shows the intended push payload without executing. (3) Every push attempt — success, failure, skipped — writes a durable record to evidence/external_sync.json with {ref_uri, kind, attempted_at, status: pending|pushed|failed|skipped, response, error}. (4) NO silent 'warning only' failures — unreachable PM-tool writes status=failed evidence, never just a stderr line. (5) `dontpanic plan resync <plan-id>` retries failed entries idempotently. (6) PM-tool unreachable DOES NOT block plan close (per D003 review intent) but MUST produce a failed evidence record.

title: Defer dontpanic adapter add CLI to follow-on plan
body: Initial draft had F004 = `dontpanic adapter add <service>` CLI wrapping the 4-step manual adapter setup. Reviewer flagged as premature: build the category contract + prove one manually-configured adapter works first (Linear, via P10 F003 → this plan's F001+F002). If the abstraction holds up, the CLI is straightforward; if it doesn't, the CLI would have encoded the wrong abstraction. Deferred to a follow-on plan (2026-05-2X-XXX) once F001+F002 of this plan close green AND we've added a second PM tool (Jira/Aha/Monday/GitHub Projects) by hand to validate the contract under multi-service load.

title: Non-goals codified
body: v0 explicitly defers: (a) `dontpanic adapter add` CLI per D006; (b) PM tool → plan dir scaffolding (Linear issue → `dontpanic plan new` from issue body); (c) multi-tool sync within a single plan beyond external_refs array containment (in v0 only the first sync=push_status ref is honored on close-out; fan-out deferred); (d) mutating PM-tool endpoints beyond status flip — comment posting, label changes, etc. deferred; (e) category abstractions for non-PM-tool service categories (incident, observability, docs) — those ship as raw adapters until ≥3 services justify abstraction work; (f) dashboard ownership (F003 adds the chip on top of P9-004's dashboard but does NOT take ownership of dashboard delivery).

title: F001 accepted by operator verification after environmental-blocker volley
body:
F001 dispatch ran Claude implementer + Codex auditor for two rounds and terminated `stopped_environmental_blocker`, not `signed_off`. The final Codex audit had one actionable medium documentation finding and one advisory reproduction finding: `linear_pm_tool.py` was advertised as the canonical <=100-line per-service wrapper but was 127 lines, and Codex could not rerun pytest in a read-only sandbox with no usable temporary directory. The line-count finding was valid and was remediated locally by narrowing `linear_pm_tool.py` to 98 lines without changing the PM-tool contract or Linear boundary. The environmental breaker was cleared with `dontpanic approve 2026-05-20-001-infra-external-integrations-bridge-v0 breaker:environmental_blocker`; `pre_merge` was not manually cleared because DontPanic refused it as not currently pending.

Post-remediation verification in the operator shell: `ruff check scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/integrations/linear_pm_tool.py` passed; `ruff format --check scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/integrations/linear_pm_tool.py` passed; targeted F001 contract tests passed (22 passed); full orchestrator sweep passed with isolated git identity/config (2183 passed, 7 skipped, 1 warning). The first full-sweep attempt without git isolation failed because temporary git commits tried to use the machine's unavailable 1Password signing agent, which is host configuration rather than an F001 regression.

F001 is flipped to passes:true as operator-verified. The dispatch audit artifacts remain preserved, including the false signoff terminal, because they explain the stopped-environmental-blocker path rather than a clean auditor signoff.

title: F002 accepted after fixing real CLI close-path defect from stopped-no-progress audit
body:
F002 dispatch ran two rounds and terminated `stopped_no_progress` because Codex returned `needs_changes` twice. Unlike F001, the final audit contained a real high-severity correctness defect: `_run_external_refs_at_close` called `ers.run_close_push(loaded.external_refs, ...)` even though `loaded` was not defined in that scope. The close command caught the resulting exception defensively and allowed plan close to succeed, so external_refs could silently fail to write `evidence/external_sync.json`. The final audit also correctly noted that direct `external_refs_sync.run_close_push()` tests missed this CLI integration path.

The operator remediation fixed `cli.py` to pass the parsed `refs` list and added CLI-level tests for close, close `--dry-run`, and mixed failure/skipped evidence. These tests monkeypatch `completion_gate.close_plan` and `_RESOLVER_FACTORY` so the real `dontpanic plan close` path is exercised without invoking the full completion gate. This directly addresses the hidden broad-exception failure mode.

Verification after remediation: targeted F002 tests passed (22 passed); Ruff check and format check passed for the touched F002 files; full orchestrator sweep passed with isolated git identity/config (2205 passed, 7 skipped, 1 warning); sanitization check passed (1437 files scanned). F002 is flipped to passes:true as operator-verified, with the stopped-no-progress audit artifacts preserved as evidence of the defect and its repair.

title: Capability manifest binding for Linear and external_refs
body: ADR-001 and commit c3c2059 establish `capabilities/*.json` as the external capability manifest convention. This plan's Linear reference now binds to `capabilities/linear.json`: DontPanic core owns the PM-tool category contract, `external_refs[]` plan binding, external_sync evidence, dry-run close preview, and resync hooks; the adapter owns the Printing Press generated Linear CLI/MCP wrapper, field/status mapping, redaction, and response normalization; the operator owns Linear workspace access, auth/token rotation, adapter installation approval, and mapping review. F003 should use this manifest vocabulary when rendering linked status. Future F2/F3 follow-up should prefer `capability_id: linear` over freeform service strings. Enforcement is aspirational until plan 2026-05-21-001-feat-capability-manifest-consumers-v0 lands loader, adapter-registry binding, external_refs binding, and required-capabilities sidecar support.

decision: PARKED per plans-vs-operator-actions principle. F003 linked-status chip cannot render: state_projection.py carries no external_refs/external_sync, and the feature self-blocks on the firebase realtime path. Parked unless Linear/PM sync becomes active. If activated, the genuinely-missing code (projection enrichment + static chip) becomes a small build feature; the Linear credential/setup step becomes an ActionItem under 2026-06-04-003. No work continues here now.
